newsitem.title: UK: SUPPLY WEIGHS ON U.S. TREASURIES IN LONDON.
newsitem.headline: SUPPLY WEIGHS ON U.S. TREASURIES IN LONDON.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were weaker despite a bout of early buying on Friday, as supply pressures continued to be a major factor, dealers said.
"We had some early bargain-hunting in London which pushed things up a tick or two across the curve, but prices have subsided again," said Charles Quigley, vice president at Chase in London.
The when-issued 30-year bond auctioned on Thursday was trading at 98-00 at 0930 GMT, to yield 6.528 percent, unchanged from the Tokyo close and 5/32 below the New York settlement.
The new 10-year note, auctioned on Wednesday, was quoted at 98-30, 4/32 below Tokyo's close and 6/32 below New York.
Further selling pressure is likely during the New York session, dealers said.
"The markets have to stabilise and turn a little higher, or those who did not get out before will want to get out ahead of the weekend, and it will be another slash and burn session," said Quigley.

The combination of three-, 10- and 30-year government auctions this week, and the pricing on Thursday of U.S. defence contractor Raytheon's $3.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering were weighing on the market, dealers said.

"Supply is the focus still," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe in London. "The market ended towards its lows yesterday, which suggests technically it's in a bad shape."
September T-bond futures were at 113-30 in automated trade, down 9/32 from the Chicago pit close.

The calendar is empty of key economic data on Friday, but the market is looking ahead to next week's full diary, with July retail sales and producer prices on Wednesday, July consumer prices on Thursday, and July industrial production and capacity utilisation on Friday.
